blocks.text: DRAFT RUN SHEET — Saturday, 10:00–12:00. Sam and Jules: bike repairs. Lee: sign-in and waiting-visitor updates. All three are initially available throughout. Six visitors are already booked; their repair needs and durations are unknown. This plan makes no new bookings and promises no repair completion.

10:00–10:15 | Safety briefing — everyone together; no repairs or parallel sign-in during the briefing. Cover safe work areas, tools, bike handling, limits of available skills, and when to stop an unsafe job.
10:15–10:45 | Repair slot 1 — Sam and Jules each work on one bike if the jobs can be handled independently. Lee signs visitors in, records needs, manages the queue, and explains uncertain wait times.
10:45–11:15 | Repair slot 2 — Sam and Jules each take the next suitable bike, subject to unfinished jobs and safety. Lee updates waiting visitors.
11:15–11:45 | Flexible buffer — finish safely, assess remaining bikes, and attempt suitable short jobs only if time and parts allow. This is not a promised extra repair slot.
11:45–12:00 | Pack up — all three stop repair work, secure tools and parts, clean the area, return bikes, and record unfinished work. Finish by noon.

CAPACITY CAUTION: The two required 30-minute slots provide four nominal mechanic–bike opportunities, not six guaranteed repairs. Long jobs, shared-mechanic work, missing parts, or handovers can reduce that capacity. The 30-minute buffer may help but does not guarantee the remaining two visitors will receive repairs. Offer all six a clear status update; distinguish assessment from completed repair.
Decide before the session — proposed defaults are not commitments

Choose queue and triage rules: proposed default is arrival order for assessment, with transparent exceptions for job suitability or safety. Decide who makes exceptions and whether early arrivals are expected for the 10:00 briefing. Arrange a brief safety induction for late arrivals before they enter the work area.

Choose repair scope and overruns: what can Sam and Jules safely tackle with available tools and parts? Proposed default: assess first, agree a bounded task, check progress before each slot boundary, and defer jobs that cannot be left safe by 11:45. Decide how unfinished bikes will be returned or otherwise handled; do not assume storage or later appointments exist.

Confirm the actual Saturday date, venue/access, work-space layout, tools, parts, safety supplies, and any costs or consent requirements. Confirm staff availability remains as stated. Gather each visitor's bike problem and likely duration if possible; the number needing long repairs remains unknown.

On the day: establish the safe waiting area; deliver the opening briefing; Lee records each arrival and requested repair; Sam/Jules assess suitability before committing; Lee explains the queue and any delays without promising finish times. At 10:45 and 11:15, review unfinished work and waiting visitors. At 11:30, avoid starting work unlikely to finish safely by 11:45. At 11:45, begin pack-up without extending beyond noon.
Editable visitor log — fill in actual details; blanks are unknown

For each visitor record: name / arrival / bike issue / safety induction / assessed scope and duration / assigned mechanic / start / status and next update / outcome or unfinished-work instructions.

Visitor 3: ____________________
Visitor 4: ____________________

Use explicit status descriptions such as waiting, assessment only, in progress, completed task, or deferred. Record what was actually done; do not imply a bike is fully safe merely because a repair task is complete.

Organizer notes and changes: ____________________
Key unresolved question: how many of the six visitors need long repairs? Until assessed, do not promise that all six can be repaired. This editable plan is a draft for human review; nobody has been contacted and no bookings have been made through this task.
